A 64-year-old woman presents to the office with a 3-day history of sharp neck pain that began during a
long car drive. Medical history is remarkable for breast cancer metastatic to the bone. Physical
examination reveals C4 restriction to right translation that worsens in extension and tenderness on
palpation of the right cervical paraspinal muscles. You decide to employ facilitated positional release

(FPR) to address the somatic dysfunction. You slightly flex the patient's cervical spine and apply a
compressive force on the head. The next step of FPR involves positioning the C4 segment in Answer
Choices: (A) flexion with right rotation and left sidebending (B) flexion with bilateral sidebending (C)
extension with right rotation and right sidebending (D) neutral flexion with right rotation and right
sidebending (E) extension with neutral rotation and right sidebending (F) flexion with right rotation and
right sidebending (G) neutral position with bilateral rotation (H) neutral position with right rotation and
left sidebending (I) extension with left rotation and left sidebending (J) flexion with right rotation and
neutral sidebending
 A. flexion with bilateral sidebending
B. neutral position with bilateral rotation
C. flexion with right rotation and left sidebending
D. extension with right rotation and right sidebending
E. flexion with right rotation and neutral sidebending
F. neutral position with right rotation and left sidebending
G. flexion with right rotation and right sidebending
H. extension with neutral rotation and right sidebending
I. neutral flexion with right rotation and right sidebending
J. extension with left rotation and left sidebending
